authority_boundary_statement: This ADR crosses two boundaries at once, per docs/skills/skeptic-review.md's Phase 0 trigger: an identity/persistent-state contract (the admission_use record is the FIRST F5a persistence this whole lineage adds -- everything upstream, ADR-0130 through ADR-0146, is either read-only verification or in-memory synthetic construction) and a coordinated public entry point with an irreversible effect (HistoricalStudyVerifier.capture, once reserve_once returns (True, seq), can never be unspent -- Decision point 8(e)). Unlike ADR-0143/0144/0145/0146, which each extended a READ path over an already-committed capture, this ADR adds the FIRST NEW WRITE PATH in the whole P7/P8 lineage: reserve_once's own _prepare+_commit+barrier sequence durably persists bytes to disk before capture()'s delegate call is ever reached. The admission_ref identity itself carries no new trust -- it is read through the SAME already-reviewed inspect_capture_admission/_p4_reference_bytes/_p4_require_issued_authority machinery ADR-0143/0144 already established (Decision point 3 reuses, never reimplements). This ADR's own net-new contribution to the trust boundary is therefore entirely the DURABILITY and CONSUME-ONCE mechanism wrapped around an already-verified identity: the lock discipline (Decision point 6), the health-state quarantine (Decision point 7), the capture-order/never-unspend rule (Decision point 8), and the provisioning boundary that keeps a caller from ever supplying their own ledger (Decision point 9).

class_function_inventory.pin: the exact 5-step algorithm Decision point 3(a-e) specifies: (a) _p4_require_issued_authority + _p4_snapshot_integrity; (b) _p4_reference_bytes(admission_ref, resolver) + _P4_REQUEST_CHECK on the runtime/nonce triple; (c) resolve via the existing _P4_CLOSE_ADMISSION/_dynamic_p4_close_admission closure walk, return ONLY the immutable canonical bytes of the verified admission_ref (nothing else -- no session, no plan projection, no transferable token); (d) idempotent, side-effect-free, no write/session/ledger effect on any call; (e) called TWICE by capture() -- once before reservation (to derive the key/body), once more immediately after a successful reservation and immediately before authority.capture(...) (the post-reservation recheck); a refusal on the SECOND call leaves the reservation durably spent (no unspend) but the delegate call does not happen

class_function_inventory.name: idempotency key derivation
class_function_inventory.pin: EXACT preimage: "admission_use:v1:" + canonical_hash({"kind": admission_ref["kind"], "schema": admission_ref["schema"], "sha256": admission_ref["sha256"]}), computed production-side (dskit.production.base.canonical_hash, NOT trust.py's _canonical_bytes/_hs_canonical_bytes) from the bytes step (c) above returned -- never from caller-supplied JSON directly. role is DELIBERATELY OMITTED: every value _p4_reference_bytes accepts today fixes role=="study-lifecycle" and kind/schema are already a pinned 1:1 pair, so role carries no distinguishing information in the key (it still appears in the reserved record's body.admission_ref and is therefore still covered by the ledger's existing same-id/different-payload conflict refusal). NO process id, run id, object id, clock reading or nonce enters the key -- consumer_run_identity/process_measurement_sha256/runtime_sha256/transition_nonces are per-call metadata-freshness checks on the AUTHORITY, not spend-right components; including them would let a caller mint a fresh nonce and re-spend the same admission, which is exactly the bypass this key design prevents (see matrix row 10)

process crashes leaving a torn line INSIDE a sealed (non-final) segment -- must REFUSE reopen per the existing rule (a complete corrupt record or interior damage refuses; only the FINAL incomplete non-newline JSONL tail is truncatable), confirming this ADR does not weaken that existing refusal for the specific case of an admission_use record

process crashes AFTER the admission_use line is fully written (complete JSON + newline) but BEFORE reserve_once's own barrier()/_sync() call durably flushed it to the underlying storage medium -- distinguishing a torn WRITE from an un-synced COMPLETE write; Phase 0 records this as the row where the POSIX flock-release-on-crash assumption becomes load-bearing
matrix.expected_outcome: a genuinely torn final line is discarded and the chain (including whether the admission is spent) is exactly as it was before that torn write began -- i.e. the crashed capture() attempt is CORRECTLY treated as never-reserved, and a fresh capture() with the same admission_ref may legitimately proceed and succeed; a complete-but-possibly-unsynced final admission_use line, once durably readable on reopen, is treated as spent (this is the barrier()-durability guarantee's whole point -- reserve_once never returns (True, seq) to capture() until barrier() itself succeeds, so a caller-visible (True, seq) implies the write WILL survive a crash, modulo the explicit OS assumption below); the SAME PROOF this ADR's recheck flagged for the cross-process lock (Decision point 6) is made an EXPLICIT IMPLEMENTATION PIN here, verbatim per the recheck's own recommendation: this design implicitly relies on standard POSIX flock-release-on-process-exit semantics for crash recovery -- a crashed writer's serve.lock fd is released by the OS kernel when the process's file descriptors are torn down, which is universally true on the target Linux/POSIX platforms but is NOT itself proven by any code in ledger.py/health.py (both merely take/release the lock in the ordinary, non-crash case) -- RED should add this as a documented, explicit assumption (a one-sentence code comment plus this Phase 0 matrix entry), not silently rely on it
matrix.forbidden_effect: a torn tail permanently poisoning the ledger (refusing ALL future reopen rather than discarding just the torn suffix); a torn admission_use line being silently treated as a completed reservation; the POSIX flock-release assumption going unstated anywhere in the shipped code/docs after GREEN, since a non-POSIX or containerized deployment where fd cleanup on crash is NOT guaranteed would silently violate the second-process-contention proof (Decision point 6/11) without this pin ever having been written down

non_goals: Editing or weakening authorize_capture_set, commit_p4_batch, _p4_close_admission, _dynamic_p4_close_admission, or any ADR-0143/0144 dynamic-dispatch code -- that route's own ledger-backed closure is untouched and unreferenced beyond the shared _p4_reference_bytes/_P4_REQUEST_CHECK/_P4_CLOSE_ADMISSION helpers Decision point 3 reuses read-only.
A second writer, planner, ledger or tape engine -- exactly one ChainLedger per series, reused, never duplicated.
Claiming OS-owned external-broker deployment durability, multi-machine replication, or any guarantee beyond the same-filesystem process-restart boundary Decision point 12 states.
Real data, replay, HPO/refit, backtest, paper/live activity or deployment of any kind.

Whole-F5a closure or unblocking F3/F5b -- this ADR closes F5A-R23 only, and only after its own Phase 0/RED/GREEN/two-final-lens cycle completes; whole-F5a additionally needs the integration gate every prior Packet closure has named.

Wiring HistoricalStudyVerifier.durable(...) into compose.py's live serving bundle -- Decision point 9's factory exists for a trusted composition caller (test harness or future work) to use; this ADR does not itself add a call site in compose.py, and HistoricalStudyVerifier remains, as today, constructed nowhere in production code outside verifier.py and its own tests.
Any change to bind()'s five retained plan artifacts, their _plan_artifact_bound validation, or ADR-0125's private-plan-precedes-capture ordering.

Any change to JsonlLedger's five store hooks (_open/_store/_sync/_walk/_shutdown), rotation, durability grading, or libs/sqlite.py's parallel store -- reserve_once/_transition_lock are added once on the shared ChainLedger base and inherited, not reimplemented per store; a store-conformance test for libs/sqlite.py is left to Phase 0 to scope, not assumed clean by this ADR.
deployment_eligible=false throughout -- Decision point 9's durable(...) factory does not set it to anything else, and no code path in this ADR reads or branches on it.

open_findings_for_independent_skeptic.finding: lock-ordering between HistoricalStudyVerifier's existing self._capture_lock and ChainLedger's new self._transition_lock is not spelled out by the ADR text beyond 'under its existing self._capture_lock'
open_findings_for_independent_skeptic.detail: see matrix row 3 -- capture() now acquires TWO locks per call (self._capture_lock, unchanged, then internally reserve_once's self._transition_lock). Two verifiers sharing one ChainLedger but each with their OWN self._capture_lock could in principle interleave differently than two threads sharing ONE verifier. Recommend the independent skeptic confirm no deadlock or reordering hazard exists across multiple verifier instances sharing one durable ChainLedger, since Decision point 9 explicitly allows 'every durable verifier sharing one root opens the identical on-disk chain' -- i.e. multiple verifier objects, each with an independent self._capture_lock, CAN legitimately share one underlying ChainLedger/_transition_lock.

open_findings_for_independent_skeptic.finding: inspect_capture_admission's return-value canonicalization function (_canonical_bytes vs _hs_canonical_bytes) is not explicitly pinned by the ADR text for the dynamic-resolver arm
open_findings_for_independent_skeptic.detail: see code_read -- ADR Decision point 3c's prose says '_canonical_bytes(admission_ref) after the above checks pass' without addressing that _p4_reference_bytes itself already returns _hs_canonical_bytes(value) for the dynamic-resolver branch, a DIFFERENT function from the fixed branch's _canonical_bytes. Empirically (confirmed by this matrix's own code_read, comparing both functions' json.dumps parameters) they produce byte-identical output for any plain dict of string values, so no correctness defect exists today -- but the ADR text itself does not state this equivalence, and a future change to either function's admissibility rules could silently diverge them for this exact call site without any test catching it. Recommend RED add a small regression test asserting inspect_capture_admission's returned bytes are canonicalization-function-agnostic for BOTH resolver types, or that the implementation explicitly reuses whichever bytes _p4_reference_bytes itself already computed (avoiding a second, possibly-divergent recomputation) rather than calling _canonical_bytes directly.

This matrix elevates it to a named row (13) with concrete RED cases (torn tail vs. complete-but-unsynced final line) so the independent skeptic evaluates it as a first-class scenario rather than a footnote, per this packet's explicit instruction to make the assumption explicit as an implementation pin.

open_findings_for_independent_skeptic.finding: no existing automated test currently exercises a genuine second OS process against ledger.py's serve.lock (confirmed by code_read: test_ledger.py has no subprocess-based test today)
open_findings_for_independent_skeptic.detail: matrix row 4 requires a genuine second-process test (not merely a second in-process ChainLedger instance sharing the same fd table, which would not exercise fcntl's per-process semantics correctly). Recommend RED use Python's multiprocessing or subprocess module with pipe/event coordination, mirroring evidence 0138's own tests_plan.method ('subprocesses with pipe/event coordination; no wall sleeps'). This is new test infrastructure for this file, not a reuse of an existing fixture.
